To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic intracreebroventricular administration to spontaneously hypertensive rats of the angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor captopril, by blocking the brain renin angiotensin system alters the hormonal response to cold and ether stress.
chronic intracrebroventricular administration to SHR of captopril alters the hormonal response to cold stress and ether stress.
chronic intracreebroventricular administration to spontaneously hypertensive rats of captopril attenuates the corticosterone and arginine vasopressin response to both cold and ether stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the central nervous system in the regulation of the renin-angio- tensin system and blood pressure in the spontaneously hypertensive rat.
the role of the renin-anglotensin system in the central regulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis.
the role of the renin-anglotensin system in the central nervous system and its relationship to the stress response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

chronic intracrebroventricular captopril treatment of the SHR attenuates the hormonal response to cold and ether stress, and that the attenuation of the corticosterone and arginine vasopressin responses to stress is probably mediated by the blockade of the brain angiotensin II system.
the brain renin angiotensin system plays a role in the regulation of the hormonal response to cold stress in SHR.
the brain reninangiotensin is involved in the response of SHR to cold stress, but not in the response to ether stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
captopril treatment attenuates the response to stress in the SHR.
the chronic blockade of the central renin-angio- tensin system in SHR attenuated the response of these animals to cold stress and ether stress.
captopril treatment attenuates the corticosterone and AVP responses to stress in SHR.
The main takeaway from our work is that

captopril, a brain angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor, has a significant impact on stress response in SHR, and that the brain renin angiotensin system is involved in the regulation of stress responses.
chronic blockade of the renin-angio- tensin system in the brain alters the hormonal response to cold stress in the spontaneously hypertensive rat.
the brain renin angiotensin system is important in the regulation of the stress response in SHR.
